## @oh-my-pi/pi-ai

### Fixed

- Fixed every request failing behind a TLS-inspecting proxy that refuses compressed uploads: a 400/403/415 whose body is not JSON, or the Anthropic API's "request body is not valid JSON" after a proxy drops `Content-Encoding`, now resends the body uncompressed and stops compressing for that host ([#16108](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/16108) by [@alphastorm](https://github.com/alphastorm))

## @oh-my-pi/pi-catalog

### Fixed

- Anthropic's `request-encoding-rejection` now also matches the API's "request body is not valid JSON" 400, which a gzip body gets when a proxy drops its `Content-Encoding` header ([#16108](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/16108) by [@alphastorm](https://github.com/alphastorm))

## @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent

### Breaking Changes

- Removed `display()` from eval in both Python and JavaScript; `print` (and `console.log` in JavaScript) covers it

### Added

- Added `advisor.continueSeverity` (`nit`, `concern`, `blocker`) to choose the minimum advisor note severity that wakes the agent after it finished with a final answer; lower-severity notes stay as a card at the end of the transcript
- Printed DataFrames/Series render as tables, large dicts/lists and objects as JSON trees, and Markdown objects as Markdown for the user, while the model sees the printed text
- Printing a figure or image in eval attaches the image to the result

### Changed

- An advisor `concern` raised after the agent's final answer now continues the run by default instead of waiting at the end of the transcript; set `advisor.continueSeverity` to `blocker` for the previous behavior

### Fixed

- Fixed context-file `@` imports failing to load paths containing backslash-escaped spaces ([#16090](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/issues/16090))

## @oh-my-pi/pi-natives

### Fixed

- Fixed native memory growing without bound, and eventually crashing the process, when files in a downloaded (WASM) grammar language such as C# were pars

Minor release: `@claude-flow/cli`, `claude-flow`, `ruflo` 3.57.0. A batch of community and dream-cycle fixes (#4210-#4252) plus a policy-ledger integrity fix (#3892). No standalone leaf republish needed this round.

### Security

- `ruflo init` / `init --dual` / `@claude-flow/codex init` no longer write a permissive `.codex/config.toml` by default. The generated file now uses `sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"`, `approval_policy = "on-request"` and `web_search = "cached"` (**standard** trust); the old `danger-full-access` / `never` / `live` file needs an explicit `--codex-trust full` (or `RUFLO_CODEX_TRUST=full`). `init` prints which level was written, an existing `.codex/config.toml` is never rewritten (not even with `--force`), and a kept permissive file is flagged with how to tighten it. Found by the three-host e2e run (ADR-490). `@claude-flow/codex` 3.0.4 (bundled, ships with the next train).
- The MCP bridge on loopback no longer accepts tool-call requests from an arbitrary web page: local-only mode now requires the `Host` to be loopback (blocks DNS rebinding) and the `Origin` to be loopback-or-allowlisted when no `MCP_AUTH_TOKEN` is set (#4226, #4243, @kevin9327).
- The policy ledger now authenticates a retained/pruned ledger against its independent on-disk archive anchor instead of trusting the mutable `state.json` alone, and streams full audits through fenced writers. Fixes `policy-ledger-verification-failed` on any install whose ledger has already been pruned (#3892, #4216, @proffesor-for-testing).

### Added

- `ruflo doctor` reports `better-sqlite3` copies compiled against Node 24.19+ headers when running Node 24.19–24.21, where they can abort the process (`Assertion failed: (env) != nullptr`, nodejs/node#65446), with the documented workarounds. `doctor --component native-addon` runs it alone (#4055, reported by @ronmikailov).
- `ruflo doctor` reports health checks as versioned JSON output (#4228, @bryanbans).

### Fixed

- `@metaharness/darwin` pin bumped
name: v3.57.0 — community PR batch + policy-ledger integrity fix

**Scrapling v0.5 upgrades almost everything: fetching, parsing, spiders, browser automation, AI tools, and docs in ten languages 🚀**

> [!NOTE]
> **[Follow us on X for daily tips and tricks](https://x.com/Scrapling_dev)**

> [!WARNING]
> **This release introduces a lot of breaking changes that don't fit here. Check the [Migrating to v0.5 guide](https://scrapling.readthedocs.io/en/latest/migrating-to-v0.5.html) before updating.**

## 🚀 New Stuff and quality of life changes

- **A much more capable MCP server for AI agents that can solve almost any CAPTCHA** (Check the [docs](https://scrapling.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ai/mcp-server.html)):

    - **Complete browser workflows**: fill forms, click, hover, scroll, use the keyboard, handle dialogs, and wait for results in one ordered sequence. Supports different field types and slower interactions, with actions stopping at the first error.
    - **Read and search the current page without reloading it**: extract HTML, Markdown, or text from a whole page or one element. Searchable page snapshots show element roles, names, and positions, with focused views that retain the surrounding context.
    - **Run custom JavaScript and take focused screenshots**: execute scripts, including async work, with access to the page's own JavaScript. Capture individual elements, the viewport, or the full page as PNG or JPEG.
    - **Inspect network activity and reuse logins**: examine recorded requests and responses, save and restore browser login state, and interact with elements inside open or closed Shadow DOM. Read recorded traffic before closing the session.
    - **Use fewer tokens and get clearer errors**: leaner tool descriptions and shared guidance reduce repeated text, while browser and request failures reach agents with useful error messages.

- **See the requests behind the page**. Enable `record_requests=True` to record completed traffic across loads, actions, and tabs, then inspect saved responses without sending requests again.
name: Release v0.5

## @oh-my-pi/pi-agent-core

### Fixed

- Fixed Cursor turns failing with `PROVIDER_ERROR` when a follow-up (a finished background job, a late diagnostic, a reminder) arrived while the previous turn was still streaming ([#15821](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/15821) by [@robfeldmann](https://github.com/robfeldmann))

## @oh-my-pi/pi-ai

### Breaking Changes

- `PI_CODEX_ZSTD` is replaced by `PI_REQUEST_COMPRESSION`; set `PI_REQUEST_COMPRESSION=0` to send Codex (and every other) request body uncompressed ([#16086](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/16086) by [@H4vC](https://github.com/H4vC))

### Added

- Added `ThinkingContent.narration`, set on Anthropic and Bedrock thinking blocks whose signature marks them as between-tool narration, and `presentNarrationAsAnswer(message)` to show those blocks as reply text while replay keeps them as signed thinking
- Added `keys.peek(provider, { includeExpired: true })` to name the stored account behind an expired OAuth token for reads that never send it, such as keying an offline model-cache lookup ([#16061](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/16061) by [@gchai](https://github.com/gchai))
- Added `prewarmModelConnection(model)` (`providers/connection-prewarm`), which opens the model's API connection ahead of a request using the same transport and TLS settings so the request reuses it instead of paying the connection handshake ([#16086](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/16086) by [@H4vC](https://github.com/H4vC))

### Changed

- Anthropic requests to the official API now gzip the request body, so long conversations reach the model sooner on slow uplinks; set `PI_REQUEST_COMPRESSION=0` to disable it ([#16044](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/16044) by [@H4vC](https://github.com/H4vC))
- GitHub Copilot requests (chat completions, Responses, and Claude messages) now send zstd-compressed bodies, cutting upload size by roughly 60–75% on long conversations; set `PI_REQUEST_COMPRESSION=0` to disable it

## Claude-Mem 14.0.0: My Work and TeamBrain

### My Work: see what you asked for, and where it stands
Claude-Mem now opens on **My Work**, a local, human-readable view of the requests you've given your agents.

- **Cards, List and Agents views.** Full-width request cards with the title, a plain-language summary, who worked on it and the project. Switch to a sortable list or a view by agent. "Attention first" sorting brings anything that needs you to the top.
- **Readable summaries.** Each request gets a short everyday-language summary of what happened and the next step, written by the model you've already configured. The last good summary stays visible while a new one is written. With no compatible provider, you see the recorded wording.
- **Live status.** In progress, Needs you, No recent update, Ready to check and Checked update as work is recorded, without the page jumping while you read.
- **Review.** Mark a result as checked yourself, so an agent reporting "done" is never mistaken for a person confirming it.
- **Drill down.** Open any request to see the work behind it: workstreams, recorded evidence and the original request.

My Work is free, open source and runs on your machine.

### TeamBrain: shared work for teams (optional)
TeamBrain brings the work your team chooses to share into the same experience: open work, useful context and handoffs, without anyone's private work being broadcast. Teams can set it up self-serve at **$50 per seat per month** at https://cmem.ai/teambrain.

### Also in this release
- Codex: skips next-message suggestion and rollout-consolidation helper prompts (#4812).
- Windows tests now spawn the running Bun directly (#4814).

**Upgrade:** `npx claude-mem@latest install`

Patch release: fixes from an audit of the issue history. Most of them stop a tool from losing, overwriting or rewriting content while it reports success.

## Installation and startup

- **Skill-only installations create projects in your working folder again** (703aa72f, #144). Since v6.3.0, `project_manager.py init` placed projects relative to the installed skill. For an `npx skills` or plugin installation, that meant `.agents/projects/` or the plugin cache, where an update can replace them. Inside a repository checkout nothing changes.
- On Windows, a `python3` that never starts (the WindowsApps stub exits 9009 with no output) is no longer treated as an integrity-guard failure; the agent retries with `python` first (e1b58732, follow-up on #142).

## Source conversion and import

- **PDF**: removed four table rewrites that were written against one sample paper. They re-derived variable categories from hard-coded symbols, replaced headers, dropped rows and invented a correlation column. Extracted cells are now kept as extracted (3aa2ec62).
- **HTML**: pages are decoded by BOM and their charset declaration instead of forced UTF-8, so a `<meta charset="gbk">` page no longer comes out as replacement characters. A guessed encoding is reported (34d88c1a).
- **Web**: pages with the same title in one batch get `Report.md`, `Report_2.md` instead of overwriting each other (e847939c). A raw `.md` URL whose code fence shows `<body>` stays Markdown instead of being reduced to the example (6a92c1fd).
- **import-sources**: `.txt` sources in GB18030 or other non-UTF-8 encodings are decoded instead of replaced (39b470fe). Markdown with the same text but different companion images (`<stem>_files/`) is no longer treated as a duplicate and deleted (104bc3c9).
- **PPTX import**: `b="true"` / `i="true"` now import as bold and italic, as `"1"` already did (8bdf440c). Page-type classification matches whole words, so "Qatar" or "Department" no longer reads as a Q&A or chapter page (c0ce2420

## huashu-design 3.0：三个方向更敢，项目之间也不再长一个样

3.0 重做了「三个方向」这一步，补上了一套越用越懂你的机制。我们拿固定题目做了三轮改前改后盲选，这一版在两道上一轮输掉的题上都赢了。

### 三个方向怎么来

- **先出六个候选，再挑三个做成真稿。** 三套逻辑（最佳设计师 / 现实参照 / 秒数轮盘）各出两个候选，先画成一页缩略图，挑最强、彼此最不一样、不撞你最近项目的三版做完整设计。另外三张作为备选一起给你，看中哪张再做。
- **现实参照改成同媒介、先截图。** 做 App 找获奖 App，做 deck 找出版物和提案。新增 `scripts/ref_board.py`，把参考作品截成参考板，agent 亲眼看过再拆网格、字号比和色彩比例；截出来一片纯色（WebGL 站点常见）会被判为「没看到」。
- **加选项，不加禁令。** 暖纸衬线、深底单点缀这类外观家族不再被劝退，只在三版挤在同一家族、或和你最近的项目撞了时提醒。

### 风格库 60 → 84 种，每种都有样张

- 新增 **App 12 种**（硬件面板、液态玻璃、玩味 3D、专业相机工具……）和 **中文与东亚 12 种**（吕敬人书籍设计、宋刻本版式、民国书衣、上海摩登、香港街招、杉浦康平、田中一光、服部一成、佐藤可士和……）。
- 84 种风格每种配一张 1200×750 样张（`assets/style-specimens/`，html 源码 + jpg），每个分区一张总览图。agent 先看到风格做到位是什么样，再动手。

### 越用越懂你

- `scripts/learn.py`：开工前带出你说过的品味原话和过去的教训，收工时记下值得记的（会先告诉你）。
- **外观账本**：每次交付记一笔长什么样，下个项目主动避开。
- `scripts/design_lint.py`：只量事实的设计体检——裂图、字太小、对比度不够、控制台报错是红灯；顺手的模板装饰是黄灯；`compare` 查三版是不是换皮，`ledger check` 查和最近的项目撞没撞。
- 这些记录只在你本机的 `~/.huashu-design/`，不上传、不随 skill 分发。

### 其他

- App 原型改成有构图的展示板，不再默认一排等大的手机。
- SKILL.md 改成路由，网页 / deck / 信息图 / 动画各有模块手册，按需读取。
- 修复 #56：PPTX 导出时 svg 旁的裸文字被丢掉，现在导出后会自动比对文字。

### 怎么更新

```
git -C <你的 huashu-design 目录> pull --ff-only
```

用 `npx skills add alchaincyf/huashu-design` 安装的，重新运行一次即可。新脚本需要 Python 版 Playwright 和 Pillow：`pip install playwright pillow && python3 -m playwright install chromium`（没有时相关检查会跳过并提示，不影响出设计）。
name: v3.0.0

Scrubbing back across a scene in the preview now shows its content instead of an empty frame. Cloud renders size their chunks to the worker limit and assemble in one pass, so long videos finish faster.

## Features

- **Producer:** Distributed renders accept 25 fps ([cc9e1bb33a4](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/cc9e1bb33a430b878af6dcb257ce5c9a70f9f180), [#5423](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/5423)).
- **Producer:** Render at 720p and 480p from a larger composition ([09c0307c3fd](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/09c0307c3fd0318a7ea77e6b41df4e5d30a1902b), [#5724](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/5724)).

## Fixes

- **Core:** Scrubbing back across a scene no longer leaves its content hidden ([4cf0e3a0e59](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/4cf0e3a0e599c73a9a96efcee8f62099323a08cf), [#5766](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/5766)).
- **Engine:** Local renders lay out width-only videos like the browser ([fc41fa277a5](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/fc41fa277a5649eb4879b524192dd6bee39d7465), [#5771](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/5771)).
- **CLI:** A browser a sandbox refuses says to rerun the command with escalation ([fa936691562](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/fa9366915620ea9baa1d03b0eb44caaca013dc21), [#5734](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/5734)).
- **CLI:** Check's dense overlap pass takes at most 240 samples, at clip windows first ([caea3863b07](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/caea3863b075f5f79d1c77dd084d05ea05aa0529), [#5764](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/5764)).
- **Lint:** Stop flagging dir on <html>; a render test now guards RTL export ([e6ce7337962](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/e6ce73379620fb2abf73e0ab681e85fd7f938725), [#5744](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/5744)).

body:
This release improves Cloud monitoring and build-cache reliability, adds deployment
automation and isolated pull-request previews, and makes workers and schedulers
easier to configure, observe and recover. These notes cover all merged changes
since 0.9.2.

### Deployment automation and previews

- **Move command variables into Environment** — review literal environment
  assignments in install, build and start commands, then migrate them into
  encrypted project or service settings. Conflicts and concurrent edits stop the
  migration before partial changes are saved. Import and saved settings share the
  same parser and guidance.
- **Prepare framework output automatically** — Next.js standalone monorepos and
  Nuxt builds retain their required workspace dependencies, public/static assets
  and selected Node or Bun runtime. Managed direct-server defaults start from the
  configured app directory; explicit custom commands retain their working directory.
- **Review older manual cache mounts** — detect duplicate package/framework cache
  mounts and offer configuration migration only after a successful build proves
  managed cache support for those paths. Existing volume data is retained. Build
  logs report observed cache reuse and build-time comparisons.
- **Catch setup problems earlier** — pre-install checks identify missing app roots
  and environment examples; command-variable, standalone startup and duplicate-mount
  guidance explains what needs attention without exposing variable values.
- **Opt into GitHub pull-request previews** — same-repository, non-draft pull
  requests can deploy their exact commit into a separate preview environment with
  preview-only variables, isolated volumes and per-service URLs. Production
  variables are not copied. Forks and unsafe shared-storage configurations are
  excluded.
- **Recover preview lifecycle operations** — durable coordination handles repeated
  webhooks, controller restarts and retryable close/merge cleanup. Optional

Thank you so much for using Orca and for your continued support! ❤️

## The short version

- **Native chat (experimental):** Review turn-by-turn edits inline, expand diagrams to pan and zoom, share chat visuals with a click, and see Claude goals and Codex context usage. Keyboard answers, an unread divider and Copy on Select make long conversations easier to navigate.
- **Shared skills:** Shared-skill installation now supports 20 additional agents, with broader WSL discovery and the right install locations for tools such as Kiro, Qoder and CodeBuddy.
- **Phone:** Workspace filters, grouping and sorting now follow the desktop’s shared choices. Long-press for linked issues and notes, work with server workspaces and browser pages, or continue a supported chat in a new terminal conversation.
- **SSH and remote terminals:** Reconnect fixes preserve split panes, paste order and managed-server project groups. Sleeping agents resume their conversations, and removing one machine’s project leaves its same-path counterpart alone.
- **Workspaces and everyday polish:** Open a website from Cmd/Ctrl+J, watch checkout progress as a worktree is created, and clean up workspaces with an explicit confirmation before stopping running agents.
- **Jira planning:** Switch between issue lists and boards, focus on the current sprint, reuse saved JQL and Jira favourites, and start workspaces from desktop or phone. Your agents can read and update Jira tickets through the Orca CLI, too.

**Native chat (experimental):** Features that depend on a remote host are available when that host supports them. Update the host alongside Orca to get the latest capabilities.

**The `orca` command on SSH hosts:** Existing hosts keep their saved Orca CLI control preference. To let agents there manage workspaces or control the desktop browser, turn on **Allow this host’s orca CLI to control Orca** under Settings → SSH Hosts → edit the host → Advanced Connection.

body:
# Build, release, and work-state visibility

## Workflow skills

- `build` delegates a coding session through `make-plan`, `do`, and `babysit`.
- `release` delegates publication through `version-bump` and `childhood`.
- `build-and-release` runs both, merging the ready PR before continuing from updated main.
- Restores the existing `childhood` skill so post-release verification is included.

The new wrappers are deliberately short. They reuse the existing workflows.

## Work-state telemetry

Adds privacy-preserving PostHog rollups for work-state usage by release, host platform, and recorded agent role. The rollups distinguish captured reads and writes, outcomes, native to-do use, instruction handoffs, and missing attribution.

MCP execution receipts also cover failures before a worker responds. They are a separate observation source and must not be added to captured-call totals.

Instruction handoffs are measured after the platform adapter formats the model-bound output and stdout succeeds. Cached context is included; discarded context and failed output are not counted as successful handoffs. Delayed or untimestamped captures cannot inherit a later instruction handoff.

These are diagnostic signals, not a compliance score. Returning instructions does not prove that a host accepted them or an agent followed them, and an ordinary question may correctly require no write.

No task titles, prompt text, project paths, or raw session/agent IDs are sent. Existing telemetry opt-out remains in effect. This release does not backfill earlier usage.

Local replay deduplication lasts 30 days; older events are dropped. Public/private turn boundaries remain content-free and prevent private activity from inheriting an earlier public prompt. Hosts without verified original timestamps remain outside captured prompt/tool totals.

# HyperFrames v0.8.167

Released on 2026-10-16.

Long projects preview more smoothly: the preview's work now follows what is playing, not the total clip count. Bundling a project also stops freezing the app that runs it.

## Fixes

- **Core:** Bundling a project no longer blocks the host's thread on esbuild ([b1cf6e3c517](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/b1cf6e3c517e227d1dca1b212e7637c19e502a64), [#5714](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/5714)).

### New

- **One credits plan.** Every account is on Free or Credits, with top-ups on either. Balances and usage read in credits everywhere; prices you pay stay in your currency. Raising your plan applies at once; lowering it takes effect at the next renewal, with a preview before you confirm.
- **Enterprise is a feature layer.** SSO, SCIM, roles and groups, audit and branding come with an Enterprise license or a self-serve demo. Trials are gone. Admins can now manage billing.
- **Restorable sessions.** A deleted session can be restored for 30 days, with Undo on web and `kortix sessions restore`. A session that lost its computer continues on a new one from its saved conversation, including images and files.
- **Pin and archive sessions** to keep your list in order.
- **Generative UI.** Agents can answer with visual blocks: cards, comparisons, photo steps, product cards, maps and figures, on web and mobile.
- **Themes.** Kortix palettes plus 39 interface themes, with a live preview in the command palette.
- **Kortix Apps are generally available**, and open in the session browser. Add any site as an external App by its URL, framed in Kortix. The App detail sheet, menu and connect dialog are rebuilt.
- **Kortix Capture**, a desktop recorder for your account, with its own area on the web.
- **MCP servers** connect from their URL in one step, with one-click OAuth sign-in. New MCP and Computer settings pages.
- **kortix.yaml version 3** is available as an opt-in: the project registers skills, tools and commands, and each agent enables what it uses. New projects still start on version 2, and nothing upgrades on its own. `kortix migrate` converts a project when you choose to.
- **Desktop:** the Dock and taskbar icon counts finished turns you have not seen, and right-click shows the platform menu.

## Added

- **Your ChatGPT plan.** The `chatgpt` provider runs TradingAgents on a ChatGPT Plus or Pro plan instead of an API key, through OpenAI's sign-in for open-source apps. Choose "Subscription" in the CLI's provider menu; for unattended runs, Docker and Python (`llm_provider="chatgpt"`), sign in once with `tradingagents login chatgpt`. `tradingagents logout chatgpt` revokes the sign-in. The CLI lists the plan's models, and reasoning effort applies as it does for OpenAI. (#1194, #1475)
- **What's new at start-up.** The interactive CLI mentions a newer release, with the command that upgrades this install when it can tell how TradingAgents was installed, and notices from Tauric Research for the running version. It checks at most once a day in the background, so a run never waits on it; runs without a terminal never check, and `TRADINGAGENTS_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` turns it off.

Patch release: fixes for work that the live preview, source conversion and source import could lose without a warning, plus a full pass over the UI strings in every language.

## Live preview

- **Unapplied annotations and direct edits now survive a server stop** (1fa3768a, #319). Before, they lived only in server memory, and the idle timeout, Exit preview, `--shutdown`, a kill or a crash before Apply changes discarded them. Closing a laptop lid made this likely: the idle timer counted the suspend time, so the server exited on wake.
  - Every staging change is written to `live_preview/draft.json` before it is acknowledged. The next start restores it and the UI lists the restored slides; you still decide when to apply.
  - A slide whose SVG changed in the meantime is not replayed onto it. Its draft is kept as `live_preview/draft_conflict_<timestamp>.json` and the UI says so.
  - Exit preview now keeps the draft instead of discarding it. A failed draft write is reported in the UI.
  - Apply changes keeps a slide staged when an annotated element no longer exists, instead of dropping the annotation. SVGs are written atomically, and a submit that finds nothing pending on the server is reported instead of shown as saved.

## Source conversion and import

- Direct PDF/document/Excel/PowerPoint batches without `-o` no longer let same-stem inputs (`budget.xlsx` + `budget.xlsm`) overwrite each other's Markdown while reporting success (8d630fff, #317).

**PageIndex is now cheaper to build than a vector index.**

- The **PageIndex SDK**, **local** or **cloud** — vectorless, reasoning-based RAG, end to end.
- **Much faster indexing** — the **PageIndex Flash** engine gets the tree from layout stats: no LLM involved for the structure generation itself, LLMs only write the node summaries, and tree expansion proposes a wave of nodes concurrently.

```python
client = PageIndexClient()
client.submit_document("report.pdf")
client.chat("What does the report conclude?")
```

Index, to chat, to agent integration, one client.
Local mode needs no server, no vector DB, no PageIndex API key.

## Highlights

- **Flash engine**: the local default (`mode="standard"` keeps the classic LLM pipeline). Embedded bookmarks are consumed when trustworthy, and tree optimization is on by default — `optimize="merge"` for the deterministic LLM-free pass, `"full"` (default) adds LLM expand, which runs a wave of nodes concurrently instead of one round-trip at a time.
- **One complete surface, local and cloud**: `PageIndexLocalClient(storage_path=...)` is the same client as cloud — submit, tree, page content, chat, and agent tools all present in both modes, so code moves between them unchanged.
- **Cloud documents, your own model**: `api_key` decides where your documents live; a configured chat model decides who answers — and the two combine. `PageIndexClient(api_key="pi-...", chat_model="openai/gpt-5.2")` runs the same in-process document-QA engine over the live cloud tool set. This patch adds worker and scheduler execution, personal appearance customization,
and managed Cloudflare Tunnel setup for self-hosted servers. Cloud spaces, reusable
build caches, more catalog apps and safer storage cleanup improve everyday
operations. These notes cover all merged changes since 0.9.1.

### Workers and schedulers

- **Run roles beside your web app** — declare workers and schedulers in
  `openship.json` or the project API. Single-app Docker deployments start separate
  containers from the app image, with shared environment, volumes and connected
  networks, their own commands and shutdown settings, and no published ports.
  Roles follow pause, resume, restart, rollback and project deletion.
- **Hand over singletons safely** — scheduler renames, command changes, name swaps
  and conversions into workers stop and retain outgoing singletons before starting
  potentially conflicting replacements. Failed deployments restore them only after
  those replacements are confirmed removed. Failed retirement of an old role is
  surfaced in the deployment warning with its container identity.
- **Require a verified startup** — every replica needs exactly one stable result
  for its container ID before optional exec health checks run. Missing inspections,
  duplicate results and processes that already exited successfully fail startup.
  Both project-defined and image-inherited `PORT` values are removed from roles.
- **Make role configuration explicit** — move and copy refuse active, unfinished
  or preserved-cancelled role workloads even after saved roles are cleared.
  Preset-only `when` and `unless` keys in declared roles produce warnings rather
  than silently appearing to control execution. Automatic framework role selection
  and cross-server role migration are not included.
- **Improve framework shutdown defaults** — Rails presets have measured stop
  settings, and Laravel's scheduler preset uses SIGTERM with a 10-second grace
  period while queue and Horizon

body:
- **Oh My Pi.** `npx impeccable install` sets the skill up for Oh My Pi next to the other harnesses.

- **An off switch that means it.** `impeccable telemetry off` (or `DO_NOT_TRACK`) stops every choice report, and nothing telemetry-only is sent or stored. Rolls still work. Your picks are reported only when you make them, and no committed file holds a key that ties a roll to your repository.

- **Findings on what visitors actually see.** Screen-reader-only headings, cards turned away, slivers and hidden forms no longer raise findings. Contrast reads the real surface behind text, including deep hero photos, filters and fades held by scroll position. Clipped icon labels and flush edges are measured where they paint.

- **The design hook stays out of your commits.** The Claude Code hook installs into your user settings, so the project's shared `.claude/settings.json` never picks up a path from your home folder. It is also found from a nested git worktree.

- **Critique on native apps.** On iOS, Android and adaptive projects, critique runs the design review on its own instead of reporting an empty web scan as clean.

- **Fixes.** `--version` shows the installed skill, so a successful update no longer looks like a failed one. `detect` honors the engine you configured for an extension and says when a file got the regex scan only. Design-system fonts keep their `var()` fallbacks, and long boot output stays inside agent output limits.

  Set `hasMultiWordQuery: true` on a trigger whose suggestions contain spaces, and typing `@Jordan Le` keeps narrowing the menu instead of closing it at the first space. The query runs until a line break or about 64 characters, typed text is never changed unless a row is picked, and an unmatched multi-word phrase hides the menu unless the trigger sets `emptySearchText`. Triggers that don't opt in still end their query at a space.

  For every trigger: while results for the current query are still loading, Enter sends the message as typed and never picks a row from an earlier query. Results that arrive after a send or after the editor clears are dropped, so the menu never reopens over an empty composer. Escape and the arrow keys pass through while the menu is hidden, and IME keystrokes never pick a row.

## Behavior changes
- `setImmediate` and `clearImmediate` were removed (deprecated, not part of the web platform).
- MCP and agent modes now load external stylesheets by default.
- Max HTTP redirects raised from 10 to 20, matching the Fetch spec.
- Unsupported protocols are no longer navigated to; `javascript:` URLs are run instead of navigated to.

## New Web APIs
- Web Locks
- Compression Streams API
- RSA-OAEP in Web Crypto (`generateKey`, `importKey`, `encrypt`, `decrypt`)
- Custom elements: `ElementInternals` and form-associated callbacks
- `Request.body` and `Request.textStream`
- `HTMLFormElement.reset`, form numeric and named index, `form.field`
- `HTMLTableElement.rows`, `HTMLSelectElement.remove(index)`, `select.length` setter
- `textarea.type`, `fieldset.type`, `output.type`; `HTMLMeterElement` accessors
- `GlobalEventHandlers` attributes on `Window` and `Document`; document named index
- Performance secondary buffer; `performance.timeOrigin` relative to the Unix epoch
- `Console` and `CSS` are now proper namespaces; more missing namespace methods

## Forms / input
- Implicit submit on Enter; improved form submission; GET submissions replace the action's query
- Fire `change` when typed text is committed by blur or Enter
- Ctrl+A selects the whole value in text fields
- All text edits go through one gated path; better `contenteditable` detection
- Single-contact touch for CDP, testdriver and BiDi
- One WebDriver key table shared by BiDi, testdriver and `press`
- Click press/release sequences shared across input paths and matched to Chrome
- Keydown default actions run only for trusted events
- Range and color inputs get their default value; `input.value` reflects to the attribute in default modes
- Skip inputs with an empty name; `:checked` applies to options; option text strips and collapses whitespace

## Web API behavior / fixes
- `fetch` resolves after headers are received; an abort signal aborts a fetch
- XHR response

# Hermes Agent v0.22.2

**Release Date:** October 15, 2026

v0.22.1 was built from the wrong commit. It shipped unreleased gateway work, and the Microsoft Store app could stick on "Connecting." 0.22.2 is the release 0.22.1 was meant to be.

> **Known issue:** Sessions that ran under the 0.22.1 gateway can't be deleted in 0.22.2.

<!-- HERMES_BUILDS_TABLE -->

## Highlights

- **The gateway starts after a reboot again.** After a restart, Linux can hand an early PID to an unrelated process, and the gateway could mistake it for a running gateway, so a supervised gateway (systemd, launchd, Docker) refused to start. Hermes now records the boot it started in, and when it can't tell, it asks the host lock, which only a live gateway holds. ([#138594](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/138594), fixes [#133744](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/133744))
- **Long local-model turns survive on laptops.** Local requests always stream with prompt-reading progress (shown in the status line), stall timers skip time the machine was asleep, a recovered local server gets another try instead of a breaker that failed every later message, and compression no longer times out while the server is still reading a long conversation. On Windows unified-memory machines, model launch and the prompt cache are sized to free memory. ([#138560](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/138560))

Below is everything in the 0.22 release line since v0.22.0: the fixes 0.22.1 was meant to ship, plus the two above. Work that is only on `main` ships with v0.23.0.

## ✨ Features

- **Release:** split the Microsoft Store bundle into its own windows-store lane ([`f9d8a740`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/f9d8a74035101d95ef2a622fb01b2f9bbc34f0ef)) — @ethernet8023

Edition 2026.10.3 adds a reverse engineering track, a third manual, and LaTeX math in the lessons. The curriculum grows from 523 to **542 lessons across 20 phases**.

## Learn reverse engineering

Fourteen new Phase 13 lessons teach how to read a compiled program you built yourself, from file bytes to evidence-backed pseudocode (#597).

- The lessons cover program anatomy (ELF, Mach-O, PE), disassembly and control-flow graphs, lifting to IR and SSA, calling conventions on System V, Windows x64 and AArch64, compiler idioms, linking and stripped binaries, data and type recovery, dynamic analysis, bytecode formats (Python, JVM, .NET, WebAssembly), binary diffing and symbolic execution, and a ground-truth scorecard for AI-assisted analysis.
- Each lesson runs real tools on its own fixtures: llvm-objdump, Ghidra, radare2, rizin, angr, lldb, LIEF, javap and wasm-objdump, among others.
- Two graded projects: `binary-inspector` (6 stages, 91 tests) and `mini-decompiler` (8 stages, 105 tests), from an ELF loader to structured C that recompiles and compares equal.
- A focused learning path and the `learn-reverse-engineering` tutor skill take a learner through the 14 lessons in order.

## Read Reverse Engineering 101

[Reverse Engineering 101](https://aiengineeringfromscratch.com/manual-reverse-engineering-101) teaches rea (`rea-agents` 6.5.0) with the Ghidra 12.1.4 provider, from the first `rea doctor` to an agent that keeps an evidence ledger over MCP. It has 26 sections in 8 parts, six reference sections, and 37 figures. The PDF is attached below as `aiefs-manual-reverse-engineering-101.pdf` (#601).

- Every listing comes from a recorded run of the real CLI and MCP server. `capture/run.py --check` captures again and compares 65 files.
- Every target is a fixture program written for the manual.

## Read the math

- Lesson formulas render with LaTeX through KaTeX on the site, and as math on GitHub (#598). Formulas use only macros that GitHub allows, and CI checks that (#599).

@SIDDARTHAREDDY8, @Vidit-Ostwal, @joaomdmoura, @kimnamu, @lorenzejay, @norareidy, @shaikn6, @zouyonghe

## Overview

This release introduces database automations, lunar dates, and location fields, expands image recognition and mind map capabilities, and further improves editing, mobile, and AI agent experiences.

### Databases and everyday editing

Databases now support automations, lunar date input and display, and location fields, while rollups gain relation item and context filters. Field visibility can be configured individually in attribute panels, and daily notes can be created and referenced by date.

### Images and mind maps

Image file names can be displayed and renamed, and OCR text can be copied and edited. Local OCR offers a choice of Tesseract or PaddleOCR, and the image menu gains AI OCR. Mind map nodes support inserting and pasting images, with improved relationship arrows, zooming, and summary operations.

### Cross-platform experience and AI

Mobile editing, database interactions, and block reference popovers are improved, along with Chinese input, search, and touch interactions on iPad. Desktop settings can open in independent windows, data snapshots gain date range filtering, and performance improves when working with large tables or deleting documents in batches.

The AI agent supports ChatGPT account sign-in and CSS/JS snippet management, with improved database view management and context compaction for long-running tasks.

Around that spine: a 600-plugin catalog, the Claude 5.5 / GPT-6 model wave, password-manager sign-in for the browser, a bot screen you can take over, one backend and one gateway for every profile, and a codebase a third smaller. ## 🧰 WebMCP

New [page.webmcp](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-webmcp) and [frame.webmcp](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-frame#frame-webmcp) give access to the tools that a page registers through
the experimental [WebMCP](https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/) browser API, so you can test them like
any other part of your app:

```python
browser = chromium.launch(args=["--enable-features=WebMCP"])
page = browser.new_page()
page.goto("https://example.com")

for tool in page.webmcp.tools():
    print(tool["name"], tool["description"])

result = page.webmcp.call_tool("add", {"a": 2, "b": 40})
print(result["content"][0]["text"])  # "42"
```

[Playwright MCP](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/getting-started-mcp) also supports WebMCP by default, with page-defined tools offered to the agent as `webmcp_<tool>`. Pass `--no-webmcp` to opt out.

[`playwright-cli`](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/getting-started-cli) exposes them as well:

```bash
playwright-cli webmcp-list
playwright-cli webmcp-call search_catalog --params '{"query":"cats"}'
```

Videos can now be recorded at a custom frame rate, and the decorations for actions are styled with plain CSS:

```python

)
```

body:
## Codex: memory timeline returns to subagent threads after compaction

When Codex compacts a thread, the memory timeline drops out of its history. The root thread already got it back through `SessionStart` (source `compact`). Codex never sends `SessionStart` to subagent threads, though, so a subagent that compacted kept working without its memory.

- A new **PostCompact** hook marks the compacted thread, keyed by `session_id` plus `agent_id`.
- That thread's next **PostToolUse** records the observation as usual, consumes the marker, and returns the timeline once as `additionalContext`.
- **SessionStart** clears the marker, so the root thread never gets the timeline twice.
- Shared session-marker file handling now backs both the Codex compaction gate and the Kimi context gate.

tasteskill v2 is a new default skill, not an edit of the old one. It gives a coding agent an art direction, real pictures and a way to check its own work in a real browser.

## Install or upgrade

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill "design-taste-frontend"
```

The install name did not change. Needs Node 22+ and Chrome, Edge or Chromium. Installs nothing, uses no API keys.

## What is new

- **A library instead of adjectives.** Built from a study of 247 curated sites: 20 directions, 48 hero compositions, 172 section layouts, 44 type systems, 56 palettes.
- **A script deals the direction.** `scripts/draw.mjs` deals three directions; the agent picks the one that can carry something only this client has.
- **Real pictures.** `scripts/assets.mjs` finds photographs, maps and footage of the subject's world in open collections, downloads them and records the credits.
- **A real-browser inspector.** `scripts/inspect.mjs` opens the page at 1440, 768 and 390 px and fails it on eyebrow labels, hairlines, gradients, resting shadows, headlines over two lines, empty screens and covered text.
- **A look-and-fix loop.** The agent critiques its own screenshots and fixes the top three problems, up to three rounds.

Across four test briefs built with and without the skill: 37 small labels and 249 hairline rules without it, none with it; no photographs without it, 48 with it.

## Also in this release

- Codex can install the collection as a plugin (`codex plugin marketplace add Leonxlnx/taste-skill`).
- The previous default stays available as `design-taste-frontend-v2-experimental`, and the original as `design-taste-frontend-v1`.
- README rewritten around v2, with before/after examples.

## Headline

v2.3.1 adds **Blog Studio**, an optional companion for Claude Code that shows your blog run as it happens. Everything else is v2.3.0: no change to the delivery gates, scripts or skills.

## Blog Studio 0.2.0 (new, optional)

A Claude Code mod that sits next to the `claude-blog` plugin. It is a second plugin in the same marketplace and is never enabled by the core plugin or the standalone installers.

- **Status band** above the prompt with the current stage of the run.
- **Live pipeline and five-gate panel**: research, outline, draft, visuals, render, review and the five delivery gates, inferred from tool calls and overridden by the real preflight evidence.
- **History of past blogs** across projects, with date, status and gate count. It stores paths and results only, never article text.
- **Run checks** control that runs the strict five-gate preflight against the selected draft.

Install:

```text
/plugin marketplace add AgriciDaniel/claude-blog
/plugin install blog-studio@agricidaniel-blog
/blog-studio configure /path/to/claude-blog/scripts
```

Needs a Claude Code release with mods support (checked on 2.1.294 to 2.1.296, Linux CLI). The Desktop app is fixture-tested only. Strict plugin validation passes and its 59 test-kit tests pass without a model, session or network. Read `plugins/blog-studio/README.md` for the commands and the honest list of what is still open (your own terminal theme and glyphs, very tall terminals, reload and resume under heavy agent work).

## Headline

The written pipeline and the five delivery gates now agree. In v2.2.0 the documented `/blog write` path could not pass Gate 4: nothing issued the review nonce and nobody saved `review.md`. v2.3.0 ships one canonical delivery sequence, gates that check what the contract says they check, installers that never overwrite your files, and CI that actually runs the browser tests.

## Upgrade notes (read first)

- **Install from the new release, not the `v2.2.0` tag.** The v2.2.0 installer predates the ownership protections; the README explains the safe path.
- **Existing installs:** the installer refuses to overwrite files it does not own and tells you what to do. `--force-adopt` (`-ForceAdopt` on Windows) adopts them after saving a timestamped backup under `~/.claude/claude-blog-backups/`.
- **Stricter gates.** A draft that passed Gate 2 to 5 before can fail now. Each failure names the fix. New checks: stale review (the review must match the exact files delivered), leftover placeholders, hand-edited HTML, hidden text, active content, and basic HTML structure (language, title, one H1, heading order, og tags, image alt text).
- **File names.** Outputs are named from frontmatter `slug`, else the markdown file name. If `slug` differs from the file name you get a warning with the exact rename.
- **Consent gates.** Image, audio, NotebookLM, Google and taxonomy skills now ask before spending money or writing to a CMS.
- **Audio.** `flash38` (Gemini 3.8 TTS) is the default, `--max-chunks` caps a run at 12 chunks, legacy aliases still work with a deprecation warning.
- **Hero images.** Default model is `gemini-nano-banana-2.1`; the fallback ladder now stops on key, billing or quota errors instead of retrying every model.
- **Scoring.** A draft with more than 20 of 100 points marked N/A is `BLOCKING` ("too little draft evidence").

## What is new and fixed

**Delivery pipeline**
- One canonical sequence in `skills/blog/references/blog-delivery-contract.md`: draft, reso
name: Claude Blog v2.3.0: one delivery pipeline, safer installers, verified CI

Caveman 4.0.1 fixes what turned up in the first hours of 4.0.0: a Windows uninstall bug, a sync that could never catch up, and problems on OpenCode 2 and Pi.

### Windows

- `caveman off --all` left the Caveman Blocks hook in Claude Code's settings, and every `caveman setup` added another copy. Blocks v0.1.0-rc.5 installs its binary as `.exe`, recognises the entries rc.4 wrote, and replaces them on the next `caveman setup`.
- An npm `.cmd` shim that forwards to a native `.exe` launches again.
- Hook child processes no longer flash a console window.

### Sync

- `caveman sync` uploads a large backlog of local spans in batches. Before, a store over the 16 MiB import cap failed with "Request body exceeds configured limit" on every retry.
- The `ExperimentalWarning: SQLite` line is gone.
- Known issue: the practice-findings part of `caveman sync` still reports "Request rejected". That is a Caveman Cloud bug and needs no CLI update once Cloud is fixed.

### OpenCode

- On OpenCode 2, a subagent spawn reset the mode for every session, undoing "stop caveman" and `/ultracave`. Subagent sessions no longer touch the mode.
- The "provider is not routed" warning reads where a provider actually sends requests.

### Pi

- `caveman wrap pi` after `caveman enable pi` loaded the extension twice and Pi exited 1.
- Routing a model no longer resets the thinking level (`--thinking high` stayed only until session start).
- Works with Pi 1.1+ custom-message turns.
- `@caveman-ai/pi` 0.3.1: the npm package now reads Caveman 4's config and port.

### Claude Code and Codex

- The prompt hook gives up after 2 seconds when the host sends no complete payload, like the other hooks.
- Blocks honors `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `CODEX_HOME`; it used to write the hook into `~/.claude` regardless.
- `caveman status` no longer says "account refresh offline" after signing in to a different account.

### Smaller fixes

- Proxy: one key sent in both auth headers keeps its bearer; a Termux-built proxy is reco
name: Caveman 4.0.1

## CloakBrowser Pro: Linux Stable advances to Chromium 154.0.8037.57.2

Chromium `154.0.8037.57.2` is now Stable on **Linux** (x64 and ARM64). Windows and macOS Stable stay on `154.0.8037.57.1`.

With a valid CloakBrowser key, the wrapper automatically selects the Stable build for your platform. No version pin is required.

### What's new since 154.0.8037.57.1 (Linux)

- **3 to 6 times less CPU** when running headed in Docker or on a GPU-less Linux server. Headless mode and machines with a real GPU are not affected.
- **Safer proxy handling.** Proxy passwords with special characters now work, and a proxy setting the browser cannot read stops the connection instead of going out without the proxy.
- **A more patient license connection**, with a new `--license-route=auto|direct|proxy` flag. `auto` is the default and works as before.
- **Windows persona hardware follows the graphics model.** On Intel graphics profiles, a fixed seed may report different core and memory values than before.
- **Windows persona fonts match real Windows by default** when the real Windows fonts are installed, so `--fingerprint-windows-font-metrics` is no longer needed.
- **The macOS persona on Linux** matches a real Mac in two more details.

Your profiles, cookies, and seeds are untouched. Only the browser itself is replaced.

### Current wrapper: v0.6.2

Update the wrapper before launching:

```bash
pip install -U cloakbrowser
npm update cloakbrowser
dotnet add package CloakBrowser --version 0.6.2
```

### Roll back if needed

If a workload regresses, pin the previous Linux Stable build:

```bash
export CLOAKBROWSER_VERSION=154.0.8037.57.1
```

Remove the pin to return to the newest Stable build.

**If you hit a regression, please tell us.** [Open an issue](https://github.com/CloakHQ/CloakBrowser/issues) or email support@cloakbrowser.dev with the site and what you saw. Pinning the old build gets you unblocked; a report gets it fixed for everyone.

Caveman 4.0.0 makes `npx @caveman-ai/cli` the one install, adds Auto routing through Caveman Cloud on top of the local proxy, and ships Caveman Blocks as a module.

### One command to install

- `npx @caveman-ai/cli` opens a one-screen setup. It finds your coding agents and their logins (every Claude Code profile), shows what it will change, applies on Enter, then offers to start the agent. Without a terminal it applies only with `--yes`.
- `install.sh` and `install.ps1` end in the same setup, pinned to the CLI this release ships.
- `caveman on|off` switches modules from a registry. The module index (`modules.json`) is listed in the signed checksum manifest of the binary release, and the CLI refuses an index that manifest does not list. A module lockfile records what is installed.
- New commands: `caveman stop`, a status grid, an offline `caveman doctor`, `caveman providers add|remove|login|local` and `caveman providers cloud on|off`.
- One config home: `~/.caveman/cloud.json`. Older config migrates once, without races, and the telemetry opt-out carries over.
- Sign-in uses the shared device flow. It refuses plain-HTTP Clouds other than this machine.

### Auto routing (signed in to Caveman Cloud)

- `caveman-auto` shows up in the Claude Code and OpenCode model pickers with a 1M context window. Routing applies only to Auto, and that includes Claude Pro/Max logins and ChatGPT logins (Codex, OpenCode).
- For each routable request the proxy asks Cloud's route stage for a model and effort (contracts `route-ask-v1`) and picks from the providers you set up. If the key is refused or a billing limit is hit, the request goes through unrouted and `caveman status` says why.
- Translators between Messages, Chat Completions and Responses cover all nine directions, so Claude Code can run on Responses hosts such as the ChatGPT plan.
- A signed-in runtime sends `runtime/v1` event batches to Cloud and respects the telemetry opt-out.

### Cache

- The proxy keeps the Anthropic prompt
name: Caveman 4.0.0

## [2.0.3-beta.1] - 2026-10-13

v2.0.3-beta.1 发布，相比 v2.0.2 新增可插拔的决策服务、技能按需选择与会话轨迹
记录能力，并补齐代码知识库的 SSH 克隆与可观测性信息。以上新能力均默认关闭，
旧配置无需修改、行为与之前保持一致。

> **产品定位**：让 Agent 的经验、文档、代码沉淀成可复用资产，让下一位 Agent
> 直接读档。详见 [README_CN.md](./README_CN.md)。

### 🧩 可插拔决策服务（默认关闭）

Skill 选择与 Memory L3 更新判定统一收敛到决策服务，可灵活替换决策来源：

- 通过统一的决策服务接口调用，内置 JEV，也可接入其他 decision API
- 配置用 `provider` 指定（默认 `jev`），旧配置无需修改
- 默认不调用 JEV，行为与之前一致；开启后即使决策服务调用失败，
  也不影响正常对话与记忆写入

### 🧰 技能（Skill）按需选择（默认关闭）

- 开启后由 Proxy 每轮自动选出合适的技能，通过一次客户端工具调用加载
- 不再向系统提示词注入完整技能目录，减少提示词开销

### 📼 会话轨迹记录

- Proxy 在每轮对话结束后，把发往上游的消息与模型回复记录到 MemoryCore
  （新增 `/v3/session/add`，写入本地存储）
- 随 `tdai.enabled` 开启

### 🧠 代码知识库

### 📈 可观测性

(#170003, #169059, #170131, #169244, #169481, #169563, #170006, #169662, #169658, #169915) Thanks @xilopaint, @k-sekula, @RomneyDa, @jokerman1302-eng, and @vincentkoc.
- **Stuck updates recover:** updates settle package-activation journals after filesystem remounts or device-number drift, ride out a briefly locked state database, stop reporting false post-install failures after migration, and reclaim retained updater runtimes that blocked npm recovery. (#169410, #170046, #169050, #169352, #168210, #170130, #169422, #170170, #169463) Thanks @patrickschiller, @RomneyDa, @SergeiAug, @angeliti999, and @Warhangel.
- **Doctor keeps credentials and data:** Doctor no longer deletes an OAuth profile when the legacy auth store is unreadable, refuses retired state before migrating the database, imports retained ACP metadata, and restores a stopped Gateway when cleanup fails. (#170256, #168959, #170051, #169918, #169759, #169783) Thanks @Yolo521-bot, @bautrey, and @RomneyDa.
- **Turns survive restarts:** interrupted turns, subagent work, automation turns, steered sessions, and node-hosted turns resume after a Gateway restart, and streamed replies from a killed worker stay in history. (#168650, #169144, #170162, #170252, #170161, #170223)
- **Telegram never replays old updates:** the first start after updating no longer re-dispatches months-old Telegram updates from the legacy spool as new owner instructions. (#170068, #169784) Thanks @angeliti999.
- **Codex and provider replies complete:** Codex replies keep their last tokens and accept follow-ups after a failed thread preparation, ChatGPT turns retry a

Astryx 0.7.0 — all `@astryxdesign/*` packages ship at this version.

This release makes forms easier to style, improves phone typography and touch menus, keeps Markdown transforms composable, and moves spacing to rem units.

## Upgrading to 0.7.0

Start here:

1. **Pin Core and the CLI to 0.7.0**, plus every other stable Astryx package your project uses.

   ```bash
   OLD_VERSION=0.6.8 # replace with the Core version your project uses today
   npm i @astryxdesign/core@0.7.0 @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.0 @astryxdesign/build@0.7.0 @astryxdesign/theme-neutral@0.7.0
   ```

   The example includes Neutral; update every other stable Astryx theme in your project in the same install step.

2. **Run the 0.7.0 upgrade.** It rewrites supported callsites, validates data-color ownership, and leaves a TODO where it cannot choose safely.

   ```bash
   npx @astryxdesign/cli upgrade --from "$OLD_VERSION" --apply --path .
   ```

3. **Check the items below.** Four need a manual code edit, ten affect CLI commands or scripts, four are visual or token changes to inspect in your app, and eight are handled or checked by the upgrade.

> **Biggest risk: props that used to be ignored now reach the DOM.** Layout, MetadataList, NavHeadingMenuItem, and TopNavMegaMenuItem already accepted BaseProps, so there is no type error or codemod. Audit callsites that pass IDs, ARIA or data attributes, event handlers, or style props only if they relied on those props doing nothing.

### Manual code edits — no codemod (4)

- **Banner announcements are no longer inferred from status** → call `useAnnounce()` from the async transition, or add an explicit persistent role.
- **Previously ignored BaseProps now apply** → audit the four components in the risk callout only where a passed prop was meant to stay inert.
- **Complete icon registries require `upload`** → add an `upload` entry and artwork to every custom complete `IconRegistry`.
- **Standalone empty-operator filters no longer save on open** → save at the cal

body:
Thank you for using Orca mobile! ❤️

## Over-the-air updates

The Orca app on your phone now gets most of its screens and features from the desktop it's paired with, instead of having them built into the app. When you update Orca on your computer, the phone picks up the new version the next time it connects.

- **New features sooner.** Phone improvements ship with each desktop release. You don't have to wait for an App Store or Play Store update.
- **Phone and desktop always match.** The phone runs the version your desktop serves, so features and fixes line up and nothing breaks because one side is newer.
- **Fewer app updates.** You only need to update the app itself occasionally.

You'll see a short "Downloading the latest app" screen the first time you connect to a computer, and again after you update Orca there. After that, the app opens right away.

## What's new

- When the app downloads the latest version from your computer, a progress bar shows how far along it is, and downloads finish faster.
- Grok, OpenCode, OMP and Pi chats now open on the phone, and chat visuals and subagents show inline like on desktop.
- Messages you send while an agent is working wait above the composer and go out in order. A message that couldn't be delivered is marked "Not sent" and goes back to your draft.
- Answer an agent's questions with number keys.
- SSH hosts show their connection health on the workspace list, and the list follows the desktop's pinned-workspace setting.
- Videos and music files play in file previews.
- Pairing links are more secure, and scanning a new code replaces an old pairing.
- Lower memory use, smoother chat scrolling on Android, and more reliable terminals.

Most phone features come from your desktop, so update Orca on your computer to get everything. See the [desktop release notes](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases) for the full list.
name: Orca Mobile Android mobile-android-v0.0.55

When enabled, admins can also report on skills, plugins, and connectors, set member, admin, and team permissions, and choose a default model for cloud agents; Audit Logs now cover more organization activity.

Also in here: hooks work again when a project pins an old Node, three fixes for OpenCode 2 (compaction cache, command arguments, mention highlights), and `/ponytail-debt` now skips everything in `.gitignore`. Thanks to everyone who sent reports and fixes this week.

# Paperclip v2026.1012.0

> Released: 2026-10-12

Paperclip v2026.1012.0 carries 130 commits, promoted from `2026.1006.0-beta.0`. The headline is that outside assistants can now join your team: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and any MCP client can connect to Paperclip as a signed-in person, review work, and delegate tasks, all behind an experimental setting. Around that: Chat leads the navigation with each agent's tasks and artifacts beside the conversation, the Connections catalog pulls in accounts you already linked in Composio and Arcade, connections carry usage instructions that reach your agents automatically, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol arrive with refreshed harnesses, and agents can safely update company skills. Underneath, Codex runs survive server restarts and model-capacity errors, workspace restore locks move to crash-safe SQLite file locks, and default agent instructions shrink to a fraction of their former size.

## Breaking Changes

- **Workspace restore locks change protocol; stop every old process before upgrading.** Restore and agent-file collection locks are now OS-backed SQLite file locks under `<instance root>/locks/directory-merge/`, released by the kernel when a process crashes. Old and new versions must not write to the same instance root at once: drain and stop all old server and worker processes (including other hosts or containers) before upgrading or rolling back, then move any leftover legacy `<hash>.lock/` directories to a scratch location. Never delete or move the new `.lock.sqlite` files. See `doc/workspace-restore-locks.md`. ([#14869](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14869))
- **Stored tool grants are enforced as written.** A grant whose `scope.allow` list does not match a tool, connection, or application no longer falls through to a broader policy; grants with unknown selectors or malformed restrictions now deny access. Review custom grants after upgrading if an agent loses a tool it previously used. ([#14915](https

**PageIndex is now cheaper to build than a vector index.**

- The **PageIndex SDK**, **local** or **cloud** — vectorless, reasoning-based RAG, end to end.
- **Much faster indexing** — the **PageIndex Flash** engine gets the tree from layout stats: no LLM involved for the structure generation itself, LLMs only write the node summaries, and tree expansion proposes a wave of nodes concurrently.

```python
client = PageIndexClient()
client.submit_document("report.pdf")
client.chat("What does the report conclude?")
```

Index, to chat, to agent integration, one client.
Local mode needs no server, no vector DB, no PageIndex API key.

## Highlights

- **Flash engine**: the local default (`mode="standard"` keeps the classic LLM pipeline). Embedded bookmarks are consumed when trustworthy, and tree optimization is on by default — `optimize="merge"` for the deterministic LLM-free pass, `"full"` (default) adds LLM expand, which runs a wave of nodes concurrently instead of one round-trip at a time.
- **One complete surface, local and cloud**: `PageIndexLocalClient(storage_path=...)` is the same client as cloud — submit, tree, page content, chat, and agent tools all present in both modes, so code moves between them unchanged.
- **Cloud documents, your own model**: `api_key` decides where your documents live; a configured chat model decides who answers — and the two combine. `PageIndexClient(api_key="pi-...", chat_model="openai/gpt-5.2")` runs the same in-process document-QA engine over the live cloud tool set. Page content flows through your process to your provider on your credentials; `doc_id` targets at the prompt level; `enable_citations` stays with the managed chat.
- **Agent integration**: the cloud MCP tool contract, in-process — `client.agent_tools()` (plain functions), `as_openai_tools()`, `as_anthropic_tools()`, `as_claude_mcp()`, plus one-call `openai_agent_config()` / `anthropic_runner_config()` / `claude_agent_config()` bundles and `agent_instructions()` for the syst

# Hermes Agent v0.21.7

**Release Date:** October 11, 2026

> Patch release. This tag rolls up the ~204 PRs merged since v0.21.6 into a stable release for the desktop app (macOS Apple silicon, Windows), the Microsoft Store and MSIX, the installer, Docker and Hermes Cloud. Full curated notes for this window ship with v0.22.0.

<!-- HERMES_BUILDS_TABLE -->

**What this patch ships for source installs (`hermes update` and the desktop app's updater on a git checkout):**

- **Updates now follow tagged releases.** A source install of the official repository updates to the latest published `vX.Y.Z` release instead of every commit on `main`. An install already newer than the latest release stays where it is and waits for the next one; nothing is moved back. To keep following every commit: `hermes update --set-channel main`. Forks and mirrors keep following `main`. Store, MSIX and bundled desktop installs are unchanged.
- **Choose the channel in the desktop app.** Settings ▸ About ▸ Updates has an *Update channel* switch (Stable releases / Every commit) for source installs, and the update dialog now shows which channel you are on.
- **Reasoning survives resume.** Signed thinking replays after `hermes chat --resume` and on the next gateway turn, and Bedrock Converse reasoning models no longer get rejected on resumed sessions.
- **Updates no longer fail behind some firewalls.** Installs on `main` no longer fetch a release record that regional firewalls could answer with 403. The stable check uses your GitHub token when one is set (`GITHUB_TOKEN` or `gh auth login`) and reports a GitHub rate limit as a rate limit.

## [19.4.0] - 2026-10-11 - "Prompt Handoffs And Cost-Gated Scaling"

> Adds **2** reviewed skills for turning a rough request into a clear prompt for another agent and for proving a data/AI workflow end to end on a tiny sample before scaling; it also refreshes the Datacircle LinkedIn lookup skill with the Fetchin provider, corrects the OrcaPromptVault artifact wording, and ships guided discovery, collections and a Core overview on the hosted catalog. Ships **2,677** skills.

A catalog release for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and related AI coding assistants. It includes the protected maintainer batch merged after `19.3.0`, with existing installation interfaces preserved.

### Start here

- Install: `npx agentic-awesome-skills@19.4.0`
- [Choose your tool](README.md#choose-your-tool)
- [Best skills by tool](README.md#best-skills-by-tool)
- [Bundles](docs/users/bundles.md)
- [Workflows](docs/users/workflows.md)

### Added

- **kernel-prompt** - turn a rough request or draft into a clear, self-contained prompt for another agent: read the context it mentions, ask one round of decisions only the user can make, then return only the prompt and never perform the task it describes. `risk: safe`, MIT, community source [codegiveness/kernel-prompt](https://github.com/codegiveness/kernel-prompt).
- **skeleton-first** - prove a data/AI/agent workflow end to end on the smallest input with the cheapest settings, look for cheap wins in the sample (duplicates, boilerplate, invalid inputs that are still billed), then scale in cost-gated rungs within a stated budget and keep a run log of cost and decisions. `risk: safe`, self-authored source.

### Changed

- **datacircle** - add Fetchin as the third LinkedIn profile provider (price, limit, request, response and `404`), use HarvestAPI or Fetchin past Up2Data's daily limit, correct Up2Data's per-profile price, and drop the retired `get_invite_link` MCP tool from the skill. `risk: critical` is preserved.

- **Automations can now set the agent's model and effort for each run.** In the automation editor, open Advanced and fill in **Extra agent arguments** (or use `--extra-agent-args` with `orca automations create` and `edit`), for example `-model haiku --effort high`.   re-probes and relaunches. A session reporting `Environment fault: <text>`

We rebuilt brainstorming from scratch so it does a much better job of what it was always for: helping you work out what you actually want and put it into words before anything gets built. The new skill asks you to describe what you're after and why, plays back what it heard so you can correct it, and keeps asking good questions until the picture is clear. Then it matches the process to the work, from just doing it to writing a full design. 

This release also adds a native plugin manifest for the Antigravity Marketplace and fixes Windows hook discovery, Git Bash paths, Hermes skill descriptions, and several smaller bugs.

### Brainstorming

- **Brainstorming draws out what you want before it proposes anything.** Its first message offers to skip the questions and asks one open question about a real moment or a concrete picture. It offers a menu only when you're stuck. Along the way, it offers to look at prior art, your project, or the web. As it understands each part, it plays that part back in a few hundred words and marks its guesses as guesses. (#2463)
- **It sizes the work after it understands what you want, and says so in plain words.** It does a quick, clear task right away, agrees a small change with you in chat, and writes a design document for a project. You can override its call, and it steps up a size if the work grows. (#2463)
- **A builder check replaces the spec-document reviewer.** A fresh subagent reads the design as the person who'll build it and lists what they'd still need to ask. Brainstorming answers what it can, makes the minor calls itself and marks them as its own, and brings you the questions that change what gets built, in one round. (#2463)
